title: 🤖 MultiMesh: instance data written beyond visible_instance_count is never uploaded when visible_instance_count goes back to -1 (RD renderers)
body:
> [!INFO] *AI disclosure*: This contribution was authored by on an autonomous AI agent, on behalf of a user to report a rendering bug found in their project. The user reviewed and approved this report.

### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.8.beta1.official [4d10419ca], 4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf], 4.7.2.stable (Arch Linux package).
- Not tested on earlier versions.

### System information

Arch Linux - Godot v4.8.beta1.official [4d10419ca] - Vulkan 1.4.354 (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) Graphics (LNL) (Mesa 26.2.3) - Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 7 258V (8 threads)

### Issue description

In the RD renderers, instance data written beyond `visible_instance_count` is never uploaded to the GPU if `visible_instance_count` is later set back to `-1`. Those instances are then drawn from stale GPU data, or from uninitialized memory if they were never uploaded at all.

The cause is in `servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/mesh_storage.cpp`:

1. `_update_dirty_multimeshes()` uploads only the regions below the visible count, then clears the dirty flag of **every** region (`memset(multimesh->data_cache_dirty_regions, 0, ...)`). Dirty regions beyond the visible count are dropped without being uploaded. `previous_data_cache_dirty_regions` keeps them for one more update, but any later write to a visible region overwrites it.
2. `_multimesh_set_visible_instances()` re-marks the newly uncovered instances as dirty, but only for a positive count:

```cpp
_multimesh_mark_all_dirty(multimesh, false, true); // p_data = false: data not re-marked
int start = multimesh->visible_instances >= 0 ? multimesh->visible_instances : multimesh->instances;
for (int i = start; i < p_visible; i++) { // never runs for p_visible == -1
    _multimesh_mark_dirty(multimesh, i, true);
}
```

So the sequence `visible = N` -> write instance k >= N -> any other write -> `visible = -1` leaves instance k stale on the GPU forever. Setting `visible_instance_count = instance_count` instead of `-1` works, because the loop then marks the uncovered instances.

How we ran into it: we stream airport lights as one MultiMesh, revealing classes of lamps as a prefix of the instances (`visible = N1`, then `N2`, then `-1`). On 4.7.2, multimesh buffers are created uninitialized (#75485, fixed on master by #120230 to zero them). After a long session, the never-uploaded instances were drawn from recycled GPU memory: huge billboards with NaN colors that the glow then smeared over the whole screen. With zero-initialized buffers, the same bug makes those instances invisible or stale instead: 4.8.beta1 includes #120230 and the MRP still reproduces.

A possible fix: in `_multimesh_set_visible_instances()`, treat `-1` as `multimesh->instances` for the re-marking loop (`int end = p_visible >= 0 ? p_visible : multimesh->instances;`).

### Steps to reproduce

Open and run the MRP (`mrp.zip` below). A 1024-instance MultiMesh is drawn red on the left.
- Frame 5: `visible_instance_count = 10`, then instance 1023 is moved to the right and colored green.
- Frame 7: any write to instance 0.
- Frame 10: `visible_instance_count = -1`.

**Expected:** a green quad on the right.
**Actual:** only the red quad on the left. Instance 1023's new transform and color never reach the GPU.

Replacing `-1` with `1024` at frame 10 gives the expected result.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33629459/mrp.zip) (one scene, one script of about 40 lines, `main.gd`)
